subject: Chained maintenance — partial availability calculation and credit request
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Chris Halpert <chris.halpert@lumenware.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: two maintenance windows + partial degradation — uptime calculation question

Hi Chris,

We noticed a partial availability hit on our US-east cluster during the two back-to-back maintenance windows Lumenware executed on Jul 30–31 (IDs in your status page). Redwood measured a sustained 5‑minute degradation that pushed the service fraction below our SLA threshold for a 22‑minute span.

Quick questions:
- How are you designating those windows on your side (scheduled vs. emergency)?
- Do you treat chained/back‑to‑back maintenances as a single maintenance window for SLA exclusion?
- What are the official maintenance IDs and exact UTC start/stop times?

I attached a short timeline (redwood_timeline_aug_2028.csv) that shows the request error rate and route-level failovers we saw. We’d like to understand whether we should exclude the entire span as scheduled maintenance or whether the partial degradation falls into the uptime apportionment calculation. If an exclusion isn’t appropriate, we will request an uptime credit for the impacted minute range.

Would you please confirm the canonical maintenance boundaries and the relevant support ticket ID so we can align on a joint post‑mortem?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0199

[attachment: redwood_timeline_aug_2028.csv (csv)]

Date: 2028-08-01T12:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: two maintenance windows + partial degradation — uptime calculation question

Hi Marissa — thanks for the heads up and the timeline.

We ran two scheduled maintenance jobs in quick succession to finish a rolling upgrade. Our operations runbook groups contiguous scheduled maintenances within a 2‑hour window into a single maintenance event for external reporting and SLA exclusions. The canonical IDs are MW‑20280730‑A and MW‑20280730‑B; official portal link: https://lumenware.status/incident/4721.

From our side, both events were marked "scheduled" and we expect those to be treated as maintenance for SLA consideration. That said, I see in your timeline there’s a tail of elevated errors after the second job finished — can you send the route-level metrics and any sampling of requests that resulted in 5xx?

I’ve attached a PDF with the maintenance IDs and start/stop times exported from our scheduler. Also opening support ticket 4721 for the logs you requested.

—Chris
Chris Halpert
Senior Ops Lead, Lumenware

From: Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.com>

Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-02T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Follow-up: two maintenance windows + partial degradation — uptime calculation question

Marissa / Ben —

Thanks for looping me in. Quick internal summary and recommended approach:
1) Lumenware is asserting both windows are scheduled; we need the exact start/stop UTC and the event grouping justification.
2) Our telemetry shows a rolling 5‑minute error-rate threshold breach that resulted in a 22‑minute degraded interval where response success fell to ~86% on affected routes (edge‑cache misses + KV target timeouts).
3) Per the SLA wording, scheduled maintenance is excluded when "affects customer routing" is not the root cause; this looks like a partial degradation caused by the rolling upgrade interacting with our endpoint affinity (i.e., failed handoffs caused retries and some 5xx).

Action items I recommend:
- Ask Lumenware for per-node maintenance timestamps + gorequests (request ids) so our SRE can correlate to our traces.
- If Lumenware treats both as one maintenance chunk, confirm that on paper — we still need apportionment if customer-facing errors continued after their declared stop time.
- Proposed interim customer response: request a credit for the 22‑minute impacted window but state willingness to adjust after joint log correlation.

Ben — can you run the token-impact calc off the attached timeline and produce a short delta for the accounting team?

Rachel
Rachel Kim
Sr. Technical Account Manager — Redwood Inference
[internal note: escalate to SRE for trace correlation]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Chris Halpert <chris.halpert@lumenware.com>, support@lumenware.com
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-04T10:20:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Follow-up: two maintenance windows + partial degradation — uptime calculation question

Chris — appreciate the quick reply and the IDs. A few clarifications before we close this on our side:

1) Timeline mismatch: according to lumenware_maint_ids.pdf you closed MW‑20280730‑B at 2028-07-31T01:10:00Z, but our traces show elevated 5xx and increased tail latency that persisted until 2028-07-31T01:32:00Z on the affected routes. The 22‑minute window we flagged begins at 2028-07-31T01:10:30Z and ends at 2028-07-31T01:32:30Z (UTC).

2) SLA language: our contract excludes "scheduled maintenance where customer routing is not impacted." The root cause analysis we have (attached) shows repeated failed handoffs and retry amplification — that is customer routing impact. For apportionment we propose treating the 22‑minute span as a partial-degrade interval rather than full maintenance exclusion.

3) Proposed resolution: open a joint uptime apportionment review. If Lumenware confirms the maintenance boundaries but logs show residual customer-facing errors, we propose a provisional credit equal to 12% of the affected-minute charge for that hour. This is a starting point — we are open to adjusting after joint logs.

Please confirm whether Lumenware will: (a) accept a joint correlation session (we suggest Tue Aug 8, 09:00 PT), (b) provide per-node start/stop timestamps, and (c) share the request IDs that hit 5xx so we can correlate to our traces.

Best,
Marissa
